headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API egress plus Plane’s file/task workspace creates default data-leak and cascading-action risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and task content, while RD-Agent runs browsers and consumes papers/logs; if Plane output is copied into RD-Agent or vice versa, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation between their shared content flows, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are copied into RD-Agent prompts or browser inputs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF either agent treats the other’s text output as instructions, prompt hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before copying content between agents.
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in prompts.
Restrict file uploads to a dedicated staging folder.
Use a fixed prompt template that separates instructions from content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, images, hyperlinks, and notes and has broad network egress; RD-Agent handles logs, execution traces, and secrets plus sends data to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs. In a shared workflow, sensitive Plane artifacts can flow into RD-Agent’s third-party calls, creating default exfiltration risk without a built-in isolation guarantee.
conditions: IF Plane-managed files or notes contain sensitive data and are forwarded to RD-Agent, leakage can occur.
IF RD-Agent processes those inputs through external APIs, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive Plane artifacts into RD-Agent.
Use redacted copies for any cross-agent handoff.
Disable external API calls for the RD-Agent run when handling sensitive inputs.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of file contents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress, but only Plane is documented as not writing the filesystem while RD-Agent writes logs and uses Docker isolation. The main conflict is overlapping access to shared external services or files, not proven same-directory writes; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external workspace or log directory, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator shares OAuth or API credentials across both agents, resource contention can arise.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces and log directories.
Use distinct credentials per agent.
Serialize writes to any shared external resource.
Check for duplicate instance launches before starting jobs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane manages issues, tasks, and roadmaps, while RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs that can be treated as authoritative artifacts. If Plane forwards RD-Agent outputs into tasking or scheduling without verification, incorrect research facts can cascade into operational decisions; the pair has no documented verification gate.
conditions: IF Plane uses RD-Agent outputs as task or roadmap inputs without human verification, errors can propagate.
IF RD-Agent emits unverified research claims that Plane stores as authoritative notes, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before promoting RD-Agent outputs into Plane tasks.
Mark RD-Agent outputs as draft/unverified in Plane.
Separate evidence artifacts from action items.
Add a checklist for source verification before task creation.
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance fields in the handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, and hyperlinks, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and execution traces plus third-party APIs. If regulated or sensitive data from Plane is routed into RD-Agent’s external services or retained logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge; the profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF Plane stores regulated data and RD-Agent processes it through external APIs, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF retention requirements differ between Plane artifacts and RD-Agent logs, deletion/export handling can fail.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data from Plane to RD-Agent.
Minimize RD-Agent logging for sensitive runs.
Set short retention on shared artifacts.
Document a data-class mapping for both tools.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across the pair.
